title: End of the World Long Term Stewardship
description: Amendment 001: This amendment provides responses to questions received, updates the points of contact for proposal submission, extends the solicitation response due date and time to 9:00 AM MST on 12/11/2026 and sets a deadline of 11/13/2026 for additional questions. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Proposals are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12363N26R4016 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the End of the World G-Z Long-Term IRSC (EOTW G-Z LTIRSC). The End of the World Project area is approximately 50,000 acres on the Salmon River Ranger District of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest. The End of the World EIS authorizes commercial treatment on over 17,000 acres primarily through intermediate harvest. The purpose of the EOTW G-Z LTIRSC is to thin overstocked stands to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfire as well as improve stand health. The EOTW Project is within the Wildland Urban Interface and has numerous private inholdings with seasonal and permanent residents. This contracting tool will increase the pace and scale of active management beyond the current capacity of staffing levels. A secondary objective of the EOTW G-Z LTIRSC is to provide a steady, dependable supply of timber and forest products to local facilities. This project aligns with Secretarial Memo 1078-006 and the Implementation of Secretarial Memo 1078-006 dated April 3, 2025 to utilize long term stewardship contracts for active management. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 113310 and the small business size standard is 500 Employees This acquisition is an unrestricted requirement. All responsible sources may submit a proposal and offer which will be considered by the agency. Proposals are to be submitted via email to Mark Phillipp at mark.phillipp@usda.gov and Matt Daigle at matthew.daigle@usda.gov.

description: The Department of Health and Human Services, Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology (ONC), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify interested and capable organizations and obtain industry feedback regarding operational and technical support for the administration of the Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement (TEFCA). The contemplated services encompass three functional areas: Governing Documents and Caucus Facilitation: Develop, revise, and maintain the Common Agreement, standard operating procedures, and technical documents; facilitate stakeholder caucuses and workgroups; and administer public feedback and change management processes. Onboarding, Operations, and Implementation: Support Qualified Health Information Network (QHIN) application review, onboarding, designation, compliance monitoring, and network operations; manage cybersecurity and incident response; and develop, operate, maintain, and update supporting infrastructure and interoperability testing capabilities. Investigations and Dispute Resolution: Investigate potential noncompliance, interpret TEFCA requirements, recommend remediation, and support dispute resolution processes. Organizations may respond regarding one or more functional areas or combinations of functions. ONC welcomes recommendations concerning an integrated or separate acquisition approach, alternative contract vehicles and classifications, commercial capabilities, staffing, contract types, performance risks, and opportunities to improve efficiency and reduce costs. Respondents should provide capability information and annual rough order of magnitude (ROM) cost estimates, including assumptions and principal cost drivers, in accordance with the attached RFI and Planning Assumptions. The preliminary classifications are NAICS 541519, PSC DD01, and GSA Multiple Award Schedule SINs 54151HEAL and 541611. Possession of both identified SINs is not required to respond. Responses are due December 11, 2026, at 12:00 PM Eastern Standard Time, by email to Donna.Sykes@hhs.gov. Use the subject line �RFI - Operational and Technical Support for TEFCA.� Clearly mark proprietary information. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring those platforms for future notices and opportunities. title: Project Engineering, Manufacturing, and Science Services (PEMSS)
description: You are invited to review and comment on the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Ames Research Center�s Project Engineering, Manufacturing, and Science Services (PEMSS) draft solicitation. The principal purpose of this requirement is to deliver engineering, science, operations, project management, manufacturing and fabrication support for NASA Ames Research Center. The contract supports a wide range of efforts, including biosciences flight development projects, collaborative science programs such as astrobiology, as well as support for spaceflight projects, ground-based systems, facilities, and mission operations. PEMSS will serve as the support for projects and initiatives across NASA, including those in the Science Mission Directorate (SMD), Research and Technology Mission Directorate (RTMD), and Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate (HSMD). These include but are not limited to: BioSentinel, Interstellar Rapid Imaging System (IRIS), HelioSwarm, Advanced Composite Solar Sail System (ACS3), Starling, Astrobee, the Spaceflight Autonomous Multigenerational Microbial Sequencer (SAMMS), Rapid Environmental Analysis and Detection System (RADREADS), Luminescence Imager for Exploration (LIfE), Microfluidic Icy-world Chemical Analyzer (MICA), Wide Field of View (WFOV) System Engineering Support, the Lunar Explorer Instrument for space biology Applications (LEIA), Neutron Spectrometer System (NSS) Development, Near Infrared Volatile Spectrometer Subsystem (NIRVSS), CubeSat Laser Infrared Crosslink (CLICK), and Extractor for Chemical Analysis of Lipid Biomarkers in Regolith (ExCALiBR), and Sub-Orbital Aerodynamic Re-entry Experiment (SOAREX)/TechEdSat Series projects. Potential offerors are encouraged to comment on all aspects of the draft solicitation, including the requirements, schedules, proposal instructions, and evaluation approaches, any perceived safety, occupational health, security (including information technology security), environmental, export control, and/or other programmatic risk issues associated with performance of the work. Potential offerors should identify any unnecessary or inefficient requirements and are also encouraged to comment on the DRFP CLIN structure, Attachment B � Pricing Sheet, any unique terms and conditions, the clarity of the Technical Case Studies and their ability to effectively propose each Case Study, and the Section M Evaluation Criteria. NASA will conduct this acquisition as a small business set-aside. This competitive acquisition will result in a Hybrid Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with the ability to issue Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) and Firm-Fixed Price Level-of-Effort (FFP LOE) task orders. The contract will have an effective ordering period of five (5) years from the contract effective date. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 541715 and the small business size standard is 1,000 employees. Potential offerors should ensure their company is listed in the online database(s) for the following: System for award management: https://www.sam.gov/SAM/ U.S. Department of Labor Veterans� Employment and Training Service, VETS-4212 Reports: https://vets4212.dol.gov/vets4212/ US Government�s unique entity identifier (UEI): https://www.gsa.gov/about-us/organization/federal-acquisition-service/technology-transformation-services/integrated-award-environment-iae/iae-systems-information-kit/unique-entity-identifier-update The current planned release date for the Final Request for Proposal (RFP) is on or about December 16, 2026, with proposals being due approximately 45 calendar days later. The anticipated contract award date is February 19, 2027, with a March 01, 2027, contract effective date. The majority of the work will be performed on-site at NASA Ames with occasional support to be provided at other NASA Centers, other Government agencies, principal investigator laboratories, other countries, and at such other locations as directed by the Contracting Officer. title: Operational and Technical Support for the Administration of the Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement� (TEFCA�).
description: The Department of Health and Human Services, Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology (ONC), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify interested and capable organizations and obtain industry feedback regarding operational and technical support for the administration of the Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement (TEFCA). The contemplated services encompass three functional areas: Governing Documents and Caucus Facilitation: Develop, revise, and maintain the Common Agreement, standard operating procedures, and technical documents; facilitate stakeholder caucuses and workgroups; and administer public feedback and change management processes. Onboarding, Operations, and Implementation: Support Qualified Health Information Network (QHIN) application review, onboarding, designation, compliance monitoring, and network operations; manage cybersecurity and incident response; and develop, operate, maintain, and update supporting infrastructure and interoperability testing capabilities. Investigations and Dispute Resolution: Investigate potential noncompliance, interpret TEFCA requirements, recommend remediation, and support dispute resolution processes. Organizations may respond regarding one or more functional areas or combinations of functions. ONC welcomes recommendations concerning an integrated or separate acquisition approach, alternative contract vehicles and classifications, commercial capabilities, staffing, contract types, performance risks, and opportunities to improve efficiency and reduce costs. Respondents should provide capability information and annual rough order of magnitude (ROM) cost estimates, including assumptions and principal cost drivers, in accordance with the attached RFI and Planning Assumptions. The preliminary classifications are NAICS 541519, PSC DD01, and GSA Multiple Award Schedule SINs 54151HEAL and 541611. Possession of both identified SINs is not required to respond. Responses are due December 11, 2026, at 12:00 PM Eastern Standard Time, by email to Donna.Sykes@hhs.gov. Use the subject line �RFI - Operational and Technical Support for TEFCA.� Clearly mark proprietary information. The Government will not provide individual acknowledgments of receipt or respond to follow-up inquiries requesting confirmation of receipt, the status of this RFI, or future acquisition plans. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring those platforms for future notices and opportunities. Review all three attachments for the complete requirements and response instructions: the RFI, Draft Statement of Work, and Planning Assumptions. title: Flight Services for Wildlife Services, Colorado
description: The Contractor shall furnish, operate, and maintain one fixed-wing aircraft and one pilot in accordance with the specifications here in for use by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Wildlife Services (WS), in support of predator damage management activities in Montrose, Delta, Ouray, Mesa, Pitkin, Gunnison, and San Miguel counties in Colorado. Flights will be required to reduce coyote predation on livestock, for disease monitoring, or to remove invasive species. Flights may not be required for extended periods because of lack of predation or inclement weather conditions, but the aircraft must be available to provide services when needed upon 48 hours notice. Most aerial operations will occur January through April and sporadically in October, November, and December. WS may have interagency and cooperative agreements with other Federal, Tribal, State, and County agencies, and private landholders, and may dispatch aircraft under this contract for such cooperative use. The government is awarding a firm, fixed-price, indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity, commercial services contract. The period of performance for this contract includes five ordering periods and each ordering period will be twelve (12) months in duration. Response for quote - no more than 50 pages Questions due by Dec 07, 2026 BY 12:00 PM CST Quotes due by Dec 11, 2026 BY 12:00 PM CST Period of Performance: 01/01/2027 to 12/31/2031

title: Jacksonville Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC) requires a contract to provide maintenance dredging for Jacksonville Harbor. Jacksonville Harbor: The Jacksonville Harbor, FL - FY27 O and M Contract (non-fed sponsor Jacksonville Port Authority (JAXPORT)) for maintenance dredging typically requires hopper and pipeline/mechanical dredge(s) depending on work location in the~ 20-mile federal channel. The dredge(s) must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -47 ft MLLW (w/additional depths for required advanced maintenance areas and allowable over depths) and to transport the dredged sediment to both a designated Dredged Material Placement Area (DMPA) known as Bartram Island and the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Site (ODMDS) located approximately 6 nautical miles offshore. Dredged material shall be placed upland in Bartram Island Cell F and the Jacksonville ODMDS Release Zone C1 depending on the specific reach to be dredged. The transport distance to the designated placement areas varies significantly, ranging from direct, local placement to a few miles for the upland placement area and up to 6 miles for ocean disposal from the tip of the south jetty. The work is divided into a base and five options. The Contractor shall be required to (a) commence work under this contract within ten (10) calendar days after the date the Contractor receives the notice to proceed, (b) prosecute the work diligently, and (c) complete the entire work ready for use not later than 220 days after the Contractor receives the notice to proceed. The time stated for completion shall include final cleanup of the premises. Base: 120 calendar days. Option A: 15 calendar days. Option B: 20 calendar days. Option C: 30 calendar days. Option D: 25 calendar days. Option E: 10 calendar days. Complete all work within Cut-17 Sta. 0+00 through Cut-41 Sta. 20+00 (BASE work), which are located within an Outstanding Florida Waters (OFW), no later than May 20, 2027.This solicitation is unrestricted. The contract issued will be Firm Fixed Price. This solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be available on or about 02 November 2026. The bid opening date will be specified in the solicitation when it is issued. No additional media (CD-ROM, floppy disks, facsimiles, etc.) will be provided. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be available. Other methods of requesting a package will not be honored. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the size standard is $37,000,000.00. In order to locate solicitation, Contractors can go to www. sam.gov and search for the solicitation number. Contractors can register to be put on a plan holders list that others can access through the www.sam.gov website. title: Thomaston Lake Dam, Gate House Roof Repairs, Thomaston, CT
description: Action Code: Sources Sought Notice Subject: Thomaston Lake Dam, Gate House Roof Repairs, Thomaston, CT Sources Sought Number: W912WJ-27-X-1CY2 NACIS Code: 238160 Response date: December 11, 2026 Place of Performance: US Army Corps of Engineers, New England District 696 Virginia Road Concord, MA 01742-2751 US The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing this Sources Sought Announcement for Construction Services for the repairs to the Gate House Roof at Thomaston Lake Dam in Thomaston, Connecticut. This announcement is to determine interest, availability and capability of 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned and Small Business concerns for this project. The NAICS code for this procurement is 238160 with a size standard of $19M. The project is planned to be issued in the Spring of 2027 with construction to take place in the Summer of 2027. The estimated construction cost is between $350,000 - $500,000. Thomaston Lake Dam is situated on the Naugatuck River and is a part of a network of flood control dams and local protection projects built by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in the Upper Connecticut River Basin. The construction was completed in 1960. The dam is located between Hill Road (to the east) and James H Darcey Memorial Highway (to the west). The dam consists of a rockfill earth gravity dam with stone slope protection 2,000-feet long and 137-feet high and a 435-foot-wide uncontrolled spillway. The work of this project involves removing the existing EPDM roof, thermal insulation and all associated components and replace with new thermal insulation and roof membrane system. The existing roof has a parapet wall around the perimeter which an existing scupper exists. The existing scupper will be required to be enlarged. The work also includes installing a new roof hatch and fall protection railing system. The existing lightning protection system will be removed and replaced with a new lightning protection system. The roof is approximately 35 feet above the service bridge deck which only accesses one side of the gate house tower. Work pertaining to the scupper will require special fall protection requirements as this side of the gate house tower is over water at a height greater than 45 feet. The contractor will need to comply and submit all required USACE safety submittals for this project. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, small business, etc.), as well as qualifications and experience in performing the work components stated above. Please include at least two specific examples of the firm�s experience performing the work requirements stated above. The projects must have been performed within the last seven years. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications, which will be used to support the offeror�s effort and their experience must also have been performed within the last seven years. Proof of bonding capability is required. Responses are limited to twenty pages. Responses are due by December 11, 2026. Responses should be emailed to: CONTRACT SPECIALIST Brian Mannion Email: Brian.T.Mannion@usace.army.mil Phone Contact: (978) 318-8478 The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Brief Essentials Training
description: In accordance with FAR 5.207(c) / RFO 5.101(a), the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District (CELRL), intends to solicit and award a firm-fixed-price commercial purchase order on a sole-source basis to: Contractor Legal Name: Sheffield Company, LLC (dba The Brief Lab) Address: 1930 N. Poplar Street, Suite 19, Southern Pines, NC 28387 CAGE Code: 69KV6 DUNS / Unique Entity Identifier (UEI): 788338528 2. Statutory / Regulatory Authority Cited This procurement is conducted under the statutory authority of 41 U.S.C. � 1901, as implemented by: RFO 12.102(a) / FAR Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services); and FAR Subpart 13.106-1(b)(1) (Soliciting from a single source for purchases not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT), only one source reasonably available). The requirement constitutes a commercial training service for which only one responsible source is reasonably available to satisfy the Government�s specialized operational and curriculum requirements. 3. Requirement Overview CELRD requires expert, interactive, in-person professional development instruction titled "BRIEF Essentials + BRIEF Communication with AI" (Executive Communication and Applied Artificial Intelligence Training) for up to fifty (50) trainees. Period of Performance: February 3�4, 2027 (two consecutive days, 0900�1600 EST daily). Delivery Location: Cincinnati, OH 45202. Core Scope & Objectives: Concise Communication Architecture: Executive message structuring using Bottom Line Up Front (BLUF) frameworks to reduce cognitive overload and streamline technical decision-making. Applied Artificial Intelligence in Professional Workflows: Practical applications of Large Language Models (LLMs) as cognitive thought partners for technical briefs, prompt design, and adherence to DoD/Army security, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) protocols. Guided USACE Scenario Labs: Applied real-world USACE civil and military engineering scenarios with real-time instructor feedback. 4. Technical & Factual Justification (Sole Source Rationale) In accordance with the Contracting Officer's Determination Limiting Competition under RFO 12.102(a) / FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), Sheffield Company, LLC (The Brief Lab) is a specialized training and consulting firm that has developed proprietary intellectual property. Their structured communication system utilizes proprietary tools, and all instructors are certified in the proprietary BRIEF Experiential Learning Technique (BELT). The contractor delivers a unified methodology spanning writing, meetings, briefings, decision-making, and strategy integrated with applied AI. Sheffield Company, LLC is the sole owner and exclusive provider of this intellectual property and the only organization authorized to deliver this training and consultation. Sheffield Company, LLC is the only responsible source capable of providing the required services without causing significant operational disruption and unjustified expense. 5. Clear and Convincing Capability Statement Instructions THIS SPECIAL NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS. No formal solicitation package is available. The Government reserves the right to determine whether to compete this proposed action based upon responses to this notice. However, interested sources that believe they possess the technical capability to deliver an equivalent program may submit a technical capability statement. To be considered by the Contracting Officer, submitted capability statements must provide clear and convincing evidence establishing that the respondent: Possesses proprietary rights to, or fully authorized commercial licensing of, an established executive-level structured communication curriculum combined with applied generative AI workflow training; Maintains qualified instructional personnel with a minimum of five (5) years of documented past performance instructing senior military officers, Senior Executive Service (SES) personnel, or equivalent corporate leadership in decision-focused communication; Can guarantee delivery of all instructional services, participant workbooks, and job aids on-site in Cincinnati, OH on the firm dates of February 3�4, 2027; and Demonstrates that award to their firm would not result in substantial duplication of cost to the Government or unacceptable delays in fulfilling agency operational requirements. All capability statements must include company name, address, point of contact, CAGE code, SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and business size standard under NAICS 611430. 6. Closing Period & Response Due Date In accordance with FAR 5.203(a) / RFO 5.101(a), responses to this notice must be received no later than the date and time established in the SAM.gov notice. All responses must be submitted to Jennifer King via email at jennifer.l.king2@usace.army.mil no later than 1:00 PM Eastern Time (ET), 11 December 2026.

description: Sources Sought Response Form Renovate Mission Support Facility (B145) & Repair/Renovate Conference Room (LRSO), Alert Facility (B1085) Minot Air Force Base (MAFB), North Dakota Sources Sought Notice # W9128F27SM005 NOTICE TYPE: Market Research / Sources Sought ACQUISITION AUTHORITY: 10 USC 2808a (Other Transaction Authority for Military Construction Projects) PROJECT TITLES: FY27 Renovate Mission Support B145, MAFB, ND FY27 RENOVATE CONFERENCE ROOM (LRSO) BUILDING 1085, MINOT AFB, ND NAICS CODE: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction ESTIMATED VALUE: Firm Construction Cost Limitation (CCL): Renovate Mission Support Building 145 (CCL): $ 31,923,000 Renovate Conference Room (LRSO) Building 1085 (CCL): $ 3,503,000 PURPOSE By way of this Industry Outreach Questionnaire, the USACE-Omaha District intends to gauge Industry�s interest and capabilities in providing the requirement described hereunder. The Government welcomes qualifications and capability statements from all qualified entities regardless of federal construction experience or business size. The responses to this notice will be used for planning purposes for the upcoming procurement(s). This notice does not constitute a Request for Qualifications (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotes, or Invitation for Bids (IFB). It does not guarantee the future issuance of an opportunity notice, nor does it commit the government to execute an agreement or pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in responding to this notice. This Agency will not accept unsolicited submissions in response to this notice. All costs associated with responding will be solely at the responding party's expense. Responding parties are requested to refrain from submitting proprietary information. Responses are to be sent via email to (POC) Phillip Wickham at Phillip.L. Wickham@usace.army.mil and (POC) Jessica Beckman at Jessica.L. Beckman@usace.army.mil not later than 11 December 2026 by 2:00 pm (MST)). Narratives shall be no longer than 5 pages. Email responses are required. PROBLEM AND BACKGROUND STATEMENT: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is conducting market research on behalf Minot Air Force Base which has a requirement to address two distinct, but critical facility needs. The first is a full-scale renovation of the Mission Support Facility (Building 145), which requires significant interior, exterior, and systems modernization to continue supporting its operational function. The Mission Support Facility has a project timeline for award of the phase 1 agreement of FY26 Q3. The second is the need to convert an existing conference room (Building 1085) into a high-security Special Access Facility (SAF) accredited to Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 705 standards. To streamline execution and foster innovation, the Government intends to address this suite of projects programmatically under a single Other Transaction Agreement (OTA). This approach seeks a capable partner or consortium to deliver a comprehensive design-build solution for both projects, potentially on a concurrent or closely phased schedule. The Special Access Facility (SAF) has a project timeline for award of the phase 1 agreement of FY26 Q3 The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Omaha District, is conducting market research on behalf of the Department of the Air Force (5th Bomb Wing / Air Force Global Strike Command) at Minot Air Force Base (AFB), North Dakota. The existing Minot AFB Alert Facility (Building 1085) requires critical renovation and spatial reconfiguration of its existing briefing, projector, and office spaces (Offices 225, 226, 227, Projector/Briefing Room 228, and a new Entry Control Vestibule, totaling approximately 2,660 SF) to establish a state-of-the-art Special Access Facility (SAF) supporting the Long-Range Stand-Off (LRSO) mission. CurrRntly, the existing spaces fail to meet the operational, acoustic, and physical security requirements of the mission users. Furthermore, the space requires extensive modernization to achieve full compliance with Intelligence Community Directive / Intelligence Community Standard (ICD/ICS 705) for Classified Open Discussion (OD) up to the Top Secret (TS) level. To resolve these operational shortfalls within an accelerated timeline, USACE intends to execute this project utilizing an innovative Construction Manager at Risk (CM@Risk) acquisition approach authorized under Other Transaction Authority (OTA) pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The Government's in-house USACE Design Team serves as the 100% Designer of Record (DOR) for both projects. The Government will advance the design for project 1 and 2 to an approximate 95% completion level, which will serve as the technical Requirements Package. The objective of this acquisition strategy is to select the single "best-suited" construction partner based on qualifications. The selected partner will collaborate with the USACE in-house DOR during Phase 1 to validate constructability, refine trade pricing, mitigate specialized supply-chain risks, and establish an open-book Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) prior to transitioning into Phase 2 physical construction execution. PROJECT DESCRIPTION AND OBJECTIVES: Project 1: Renovate Mission Support Center, Building 145 This project involves complete renovation and conversion of roughly 28,000 SF of the 45,236 SF facility into a centralized point for mission support functions for all airman, families, and retirees. General Demolition & Hazardous Abatement: Wall to wall, as required to implement the new layout and update dated systems. This includes but is not limited to the following: masonry and/or steel-studs walls; flooring, interior doors, and abandoned equipment; water, sewer and venting lines; electrical conductors and panels; HVAC distribution and equipment systems; and exterior doors & windows. All abandoned construction debris and equipment be to be recycled and/or disposed of off-site. Removal and disposal asbestos and other hazardous materials. Entry Control Vestibules: as required, replace entry/exit flow and ADA compliance, to accommodate fire alarm panels, and to account for any loading/unloading requirements. Mechanical: Update water lines and PIV to ensure they can independently support the fire suppression system, building conversion, and increased occupant load. Update all restroom plumbing, fixtures, exhaust system, and below grade plumbing, as required to support the new building occupant loads and revised layouts. Electrical Utility Systems: Update electrical, including subpanels, transformer(s), MDP, and switch gear. Demo existing electrical conductors, conduit, and grounding system on the Power Distribution System as required. Install emergency LED lighting in compliance with UFC 3-600-01.) Demolish interior and exterior lighting and replace with LED lights per UFC 3-530-01. Provide electrical load analysis to ensure maximum flexibility for future system changes. Civil: Replace/evaluate the exterior utility connections and site conditions. This includes but is not limited to the following: sanitary sewer, water supply, electrical feeds, site lighting, site drainage, and communications. Provide new communications feeds into separate and new COMM rooms. Update parking requirements are needed to serve the new workforce and guest occupant loads. Additional site work, including paving and utilities, is also required. Project 2: Convert Conference Room to Special Access Facility (SAF), Building 1085 This project provides for the complete architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, and physical security renovation of approximately 2,660 SF on the second floor of Building 1085 (Area #1) at Minot AFB, North Dakota. The project will convert existing non-compliant spaces into an accredited, modern Special Access Facility (SAF) / Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) with an integrated Entry Control Vestibule, Briefing Room, Projector

title: Fort Meade Hazardous Waste Disposal Contract
description: Fort Meade HW Disposal Contract. THE INTENT OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS TO IDENTIFY QUALIFIED SMALL BUSINESSES, specifically 8(a), HUBZone, woman-owned, and service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, for the requirement described below. The intent of this Sources Sought is to identify capable small business that can perform with limitations on subcontracting. The scope of work requires the transportation and disposal of RCRA Hazardous wastes, non-RCRA wastes, Batteries, Corrosive waste, Compressed Gas Cylinders, Flammable waste, Demil-required waste, State-Regulated waste, Non-Hazardous Waste, Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCBs), AFFF and other PFAS-related waste, Mandatory Recycling waste, Reactive waste, and Toxic waste located on or around military installations or within a 50-mile radius of any pickup/service location listed on the Pickup and Service Locations Table (See Attachment 3) of the contract in the states of Maryland, Virgina, Delaware, and the District of Columbia. Infectious Medical Waste, Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Controlled Substances, Radioactive Waste, Ammunition and explosives, will not be included under this contract. Special services will be required such as sampling and analysis, industrial cleaning services, lab packs/loose packs, rolloff box rentals, vacuum box rentals, FRAC Tank rentals, and expedited removals and performance. This scope also encompasses the provision of various supplies upon government request. All services necessary for the collection, storage, processing, removal, transportation, final treatment and disposal of waste shall be in accordance with all local, state, Department of Defense, and Federal laws and regulations. FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (FEB 2023) CLASS DEVIATION 2021-O0008 states the Offeror/Contractor agrees to not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Contractors may be subject to a minimum $500,000 fine if awarded a contract with this clause and don�t meet the requirement. We have identified the majority of RCRA TSDFs (Treatment, Storage, Disposal Facilities) in the industry as large businesses. All TSDFs used during the performance of this contract must be approved and listed on the Qualified Facilities List located at the following website: https://www.dla.mil/Disposition-Services/Offers/Hazardous-Waste-Disposal/Qualified-Facilities-List/ Given there is a lack of small business ownership of TSDFs and that disposal costs make up a large portion of the contract dollar value, there is a reasonable probability that a small business would pay more than 50% of the cost of the contract to large businesses. *The Government intends to solicit proposals on SAM.gov and award a Firm-Fixed Priced, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity Services Contract. The contract is anticipated to have one 30-month base period, followed by one 30-month option period. There is no solicitation available at this time. However, attached is a DRAFT Price Schedule, DRAFT PWS, and Anticipated Pickup Points that firms responding to this Sources Sought should use to help determine if they would be able to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting requirements. IF YOUR FIRM IS CAPABLE OF PERFORMING THE REQUESTED SERVICES, WITHOUT THE LIMITATIONS ON SUBCONTRACTING, THE CAPABILITIES PACKAGE DETAILED BELOW IS NOT REQUIRED. In accordance with FAR 6.101(a), with certain limited exceptions, contracting officers shall promote and provide for full and open competition in soliciting offers and awarding Government contracts. If your firm would like to respond to this Sources Sought, but is unable to meet the limitations on subcontracting, please email Raymond.empie@dla.mil with �Fort Meade - SOURCES SOUGHT HAZ� in the subject line, stating your firms� Notification of Interest (a capabilities package is not required). SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested firms must demonstrate their ability to perform the requested services, described above, by submitting a brief capabilities package (no more than three pages in length, single-spaced, 12-point font minimum). This documentation shall identify, at a minimum: (1) Company name, office location(s), CAGE Code, and a statement identifying small business category and current status of the small business classification; (2) Relevant experience within the last five years, including any contract number(s), names of individuals responsible for the referenced contracts/projects, and current telephone numbers for those individuals; if you were a subcontractor, identify the work you actually performed as the sub-contractor; and (3) A statement identifying your firm�s ability to perform in accordance with FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (CLASS DEVIATION 2021-O0008), as well as an explanation of how you would be able to comply with this requirement if you are a small business of any type considering the disposal requirements within the draft price schedule that is anticipated to be included in the contract; (note: large business respondents do not need to address this). (4) A listing of TSDFs your firm would use during the performance of this contract, identifying each TSDF as similarly situated or not as your firm. The submittal package must be emailed to Raymond.empie@dla.mil. with �Fort Meade - SOURCES SOUGHT HAZ WASTE� in the subject line. The submittal package must be received no later than 1400 EST, Friday-December 11, 2026 LATE RESPONSES WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. Upon review of industry response to this Sources Sought, the Government will determine whether a set-aside acquisition is in the Government's best interest. If an unrestricted solicitation is issued, then the Class Deviation 2021-O0008 Limitations on Subcontracting would not apply. All responsible firms, including small businesses, are eligible to submit a proposal in response to an unrestricted solicitation. A response to this Sources Sought will not be considered an adequate response to any forthcoming solicitation announcement. The Government WILL NOT provide a debriefing on the results of the survey. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought notice or any follow-up information requests. All information submitted will be held in a confidential manner and will only be used for the purpose intended.

title: RFI-RAISED FLOORING-MARKET RESEARCH
description: REQUIREMENT: The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Region 10, Bothell, Washington, is issuing an RFI to conduct market research, obtain pricing information, and identify qualified participants capable of supporting the requirement for design services related to a proposed 3-inch raised flooring system in the FEMA Region 10 Regional Response Coordination Center (RRCC) at the Federal Regional Center and in accordance with the attached Performance Statement (PWS). The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction.. This RFI is issued solely for market research and informational purposes and does not constitute an invitation for quotation, request for proposal or request for quotation, nor will responses be considered offers or result in a binding contract. It does not guarantee the future issuance of an opportunity notice, nor does it commit the government to execute an agreement or pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in responding to this notice. The U.S. Government will not provide reimbursement for any information that may be submitted in response to this RFI. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. Respondents will not be notified of any results derived from a review of the information provided; however, information gathered may be utilized for technical and acquisition purposes. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: FEMA Region 10, Federal Regional Center (FRC) Region 10, 130 228th St SW, Bothell, WA 98021 Minimum Requirements: Interested offerors are required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). Information regarding SAM registration is available at https://www.sam.gov/portal/public/SAM SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: FEMA Region 10 seeks information from firms with capabilities, experience, and resources necessary to meet or exceed the stated requirements to perform design services related to a proposed 3-inch raised flooring system. Capability Statement Submission Requirements Interested businesses are requested to submit a Capability Statement demonstrating their ability to fulfill the Government�s needs. Submissions must include the following information: Company Information Company Name, Address, and Website. Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, and Email). Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code. Business Size and Socio-Economic Status under NAICS 337215 (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business [SDVOSB], Women-Owned Small Business [WOSB], 8(a), HUBZone). Specify if your firm holds any Federal contract vehicles (e.g., GSA MAS, 8(a) STARS III, or regional IDIQs) that cover these types of commercial flooring installations. Capabilities and Experience List any relevant qualifications or credentials Description of experience providing design services related to a proposed 3-inch raised flooring system of similar size and scope List of relevant contracts (government or commercial), including contract value and period of performance Key personnel qualifications Technical Approach Overview of proposed approach to raised flooring (preventive, corrective, emergency maintenance) Use of technology (e.g., CMMS, energy management, automation). Quality assurance and performance metrics Innovative Technologies: Describe any innovative materials, methods, or technologies your firm could propose for a project of this scale that could lead to cost savings, schedule acceleration, or enhanced facility performance and resilience. Barriers to Innovation: What commercial or Government-imposed barriers currently make it difficult to propose or implement innovative construction technologies? How could the flexibility of an OTA help overcome these barriers? Pricing and Contract Structure Typical pricing models (firm-fixed price, time & materials, cost-plus), Estimated total cost for the design and CAD drawing services Recommendations for contract length, incentives, and performance-based measures Estimated labor categories, hourly rates, and total labor hours required for the assessment, design, and CAD drawing effort Additional Information � Suggestions for improving the scope of work or performance requirements � Potential risks or challenges and recommended mitigation strategies � Any other relevant information or recommendations Response Submission Instructions � Responses should be sent via email to nila.patel@fema.dhs.gov � Proprietary information should be clearly marked. Responses received after the deadline or without the required information will not be considered. Since this is a request for information/market research announcement only, evaluation letters will not be issued to any respondent. This RFI will be posted for 15 days, or until sufficient responses have been received. Questions: Direct any questions regarding this RFI to nila.patel@fema.dhs.gov. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. DISCLAIMER: This RFI is for market research only and does not commit the Government to any contractual action. All responses are voluntary, and the Government is not obligated to any costs associated to a submitted response to this announcement.

title: Mission Module Solicitation
description: *****AMENDMENT 0001 Dated 11/18/2026***** The purpose of this amendment is to:(1) extend the proposal submission date to Friday 11 December 2026, (2) Update Section C NAVSEA Clause 215-H002 CONTRACTOR PROPOSAL (NAVSEA) (OCT 2018) (a) NAVSEA Solicitation No: to remove N6133126R3111 and insert N6133127R0006, (3) Update Section F - F.1 PLACE OF PERFORMANCE to remove Dahlgren and insert Panama City, (4) Upload Attachment J.12 Wage Determinations, (5) Update Section J Attachment J.1 Performance Work Statement (PWS) Section 3.0(e) by removing the sentence NSWC PCD will not provide space onboard NSWC PCD or the Naval Support Activity Panama City (NSAPC) during performance of this task order and replace it with PWS Section 3.0 (e) The Government will provide space for up to 15 Contractor personnel in office or working spaces each with a phone and Navy and Marine Corps Intranet (NMCI) computer with network connection., and (6)Update Section L - 2.5 from Company_Volume_III _Past Performance Reference for N61331-26-R-3111 to Company_Volume_III _Past Performance Reference for N61331-27-R-0006. ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ **Original Post*** **ONLY SEAPORT MAC HOLDERS ARE ELIGIBLE FOR AWARD UNDER THIS SOLICITATION.*** Request for Proposal (RFP) (N6133127R0006) under the Seaport NxG Multiple Award Contract (MAC), for Mission Module Engineering and Technical Support. This effort has been previously been posted under the Opportunities page as the following: Sources Sought Notice (N6133126SNQ27), dated (Posted 7 May 2026) and the follow-up Advance Planning Notice/Pre-Solicitation Notice dated (16 June 2026). ***RESPONSES MUST BE SUBMITTED VIA THE PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE.*** ***ALL DOCUMENTS ARE AVAILABLE WITHIN THE PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE*** Questions and Answers WILL TAKE PLACE THROUGH PIEE MODULE AND POSTED TO PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE BY ATTACHMENT***This is a solicitation for SEAPORT MAC HOLDERS ONLY. This solicitation is to provide services to support the Naval Surface Warfare Center Panama City Division (NSWC PCD) Modular Integration Division as the lead for engineering, analysis, and planning support for the modularization of off-board systems in support of the littoral warfare mission area. The requirements will include systems engineering, packaging and handling of off-board system hardware, system integration of legacy and emerging littoral mission systems, sea frame integration of mission modules, development of mission system common computing environments (e.g. Mission Package Computing Environment (MPCE)) and integrated communications networks (e.g. Multiple Vehicle Communication System(MVCS)), distributed engineering testing, and supporting the Government in validation and verification. Specifically, these requirements include the general program, engineering, technical, and integrated logistics support requirements for the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS)Mission Modules (MM) program at NSWC PCD.

title: FIID Advanced Anti-Fraud and Risk-Modeling Proof of Concept
description: FEMA�s Fraud Investigations and Inspections Division (FIID), in coordination with the Office of the Chief Component Procurement Officer (OCCPO), is conducting market research to identify commercially available advanced anti-fraud and entity-risk modeling solutions for a potential competitive, multi-vendor Proof of Concept (POC). The POC would assess vendors� ability to identify potentially high-risk business entities using authorized data sources, fraud-risk indicators, and analytical methods, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, predictive analytics, rules engines, entity resolution, anomaly detection, graph and network analytics, identity and business verification, and optical character recognition. FEMA seeks scalable solutions that accurately identify potential risk while minimizing false positives and false negatives; provide transparent, reviewable explanations for alerts, risk scores, and entity assessments; integrate with cloud, hybrid, API-based, and batch-processing government environments; and support applicable federal security, privacy, accessibility, records-management, and data-governance requirements. The POC would be limited to evaluating technical capabilities and would not include live operational screening, grant eligibility determinations, adverse-action recommendations, or decisions affecting an individual�s or entity�s rights, benefits, eligibility, or safety. 1. Business Judgment Guidance for Prospective Offerors This notice is published to encourage open competition and to assist prospective offerors in determining if this requirement matches their technical capabilities. Who Should Respond: Vendors with demonstrated, scalable expertise in deploying enterprise-grade predictive analytics, anti-fraud algorithms, and network graph analysis in financial, commercial, or federal regulatory environments. Solicitation Request: A formal solicitation is not currently available. Responses to this RFI will directly shape the acquisition strategy and technical requirements for the competitive Proof of Concept phase.. 2. Attachments and Links Further program documentation, templates, and the RFI packet are attached to this notice on SAM.gov.

title: Solicitation: Construct Combat Rescue Helicopter Flight Simulator Facility at Moffett ANGB
description: The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, to include all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) Operational Flight Trainer (OFT) simulator facility at Moffett Air National Guard Base (ANGB), Mountain View, California. This project will provide an approximately 8,202 gross square foot building consisting of a multi-story, high bay area to house the CRH-OFT simulator, with a single-story area containing CRH mission planning, briefing and debriefing rooms, administrative areas for training and support staff, OFT maintenance and parts storage rooms, secure and non-secure telecommunication rooms, latrine facilities and mechanical, electrical and utility support rooms utilizing conventional design and construction. The building will be of permanent construction with electrical, mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, wet sprinkler fire suppression, fire detection, access control, direct digital control, and utility management. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Air space and insulation to be located inside the cavity wall to meet Energy Code requirements. The primary roofing materials will be standing seam metal roofing to match other installation facilities and the perimeter sloped roof design will include a prefinished standing seam metal roof panel system over rigid insulation. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Main entrance doors will be a pair of anodized aluminum storefront entrance doors with insulating glass including a sidelight. The Mechanical, Electrical, Sim Bay and secondary egress doors will be painted, insulated hollow metal door and frames with controlled access. Antiterrorism/Force Protection elements are incorporated. Supporting facilities include landscaping, utilities, pavements, storm drainage, sanitary sewer, site improvements, communications support, cybersecurity control systems, and tempest security.

description: Page 7 of 7 REQUEST FOR INFORMATION THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Veterans Health Administration (VHA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) as market research to determine the availability of vendors that can provide a Utilization Management Software Tool with VHA enterprise-wide licensing that includes unlimited use, updates, and clinical and technical support for evidence-based criteria and the associated tools identified in the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) that interface seamlessly into the National Utilization Management Integration (NUMI) application and the Electronic Health Record (EHR). In addition, the Contractor shall provide training to certify and maintain certification for trainers throughout the VHA.. The VHA s Utilization Management (UM) Program focuses on using resources efficiently and ensuring that every Veteran receives consistent reliable, high-quality care in the optimal setting and at appropriate care delivery intervals. The objective of the UM program is to provide the correct care, for the right patient, at the best time and for the proper reasons using evidence-based practice and continuous measurement and improvement. title: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE TO IDENTIFY POTENTIALLY CAPABLE, INTERESTED PARTIES FOR BIOSPECIMEN COLLECTION AND BIOBANKING SERVICES
description: TYPE OF NOTICE: This is a Sources Sought Notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) Office of Acquisitions and Logistics Management, on behalf of the National Cancer Institute�s (NCI�s) Division of Cancer Treatment and Diagnosis (DCTD), is issuing this Sources Sought Notice to conduct market research and identify interested and capable parties, including both large and small businesses, that have the resources and expertise to support biospecimen collection, biobanking, and related services. The required services will support cancer research across the United States by providing specialized expertise to identify, establish, and manage clinical sites across the nation to engage and enroll cancer patients onto NCI biospecimen collection protocols, collect biospecimens and associated medical data, and to provide biorepository services. Research studies may include, but are not limited to, development of patient-derived animal models, tumor characterization, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic studies, assay development and validation, clinical testing, and collection and management of biospecimens for future use. The Government intends to procure these specialized services through a competitive acquisition. BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE (MARKET RESEARCH), all Small Business Set-Aside categories will be considered for this procurement. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Performance of services for this effort will primarily take place at Contractor and/or Subcontractor facilities. DISCLAIMER:THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A �REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)�. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS NOTICE IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. RESPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ), INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) OR RFP, IF ISSUED. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WILL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE GOVERNMENT-WIDE POINT OF ENTRY (GPE). IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT. THE GOVERNMENT RESERVES THE RIGHT TO USE INFORMATION PROVIDED BY RESPONDENTS FOR ANY PURPOSE DEEMED NECESSARY AND LEGALLY APPROPRIATE. ANY ORGANIZATION RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE SHOULD ENSURE THAT ITS RESPONSE IS COMPLETE AND SUFFICIENTLY DETAILED TO ALLOW THE GOVERNMENT TO DETERMINE THE ORGANIZATION'S QUALIFICATIONS TO PERFORM THE WORK. PROGRAM BACKGROUND: NCI uses research biospecimens including tissues, blood, and other bodily fluids donated by patients as part of scientific research to develop novel diagnostics and therapies for cancer. The Contractor shall be responsible for providing services to identify and engage clinical sites in conducting NCI biospecimen collection studies and to provide biorepository services for concurrent multi-disciplinary studies and diverse study designs. Biospecimens and associated data of known quality are a critical resource for research that investigates the causes, biology, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of cancer. NCI requires biospecimens for research purposes that may include, but are not limited to, the following: development of patient-derived models, characterization of tumors using clinical- and research-grade sequencing, proteomics studies, pharmacodynamic studies, development and validation of clinical assays, performance of clinical testing and return of clinical test results to providers and patients, and development of research reserves of biospecimens for future research use. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: The objective of any potential contract is to obtain specialized services for the identification and coordination of clinical sites in the management of specific NCI biospecimen collection studies and the collection, processing, storage, and distribution of biospecimens and associated data for current and future cancer research. For specific details under each domain, please reference the draft Statement of Work which accompanies announcement. The Government encourages feedback from respondents in their capability submissions (i.e., comments, suggestions, recommendations) on the draft Statement of Work that would improve the understanding of the requirements for this anticipated acquisition. NCI is seeking the following information from respondents regarding strategies as well as explicit examples of how they would propose to support NCI initiatives in one or more of the following services areas: DOMAIN 1: CLINICAL SITE IDENTIFICATION AND ONBOARDING, CLINICAL SITE MANAGEMENT, TRAINING, PROVISION OF KITS, AND IDENTIFICATION OF EXISTING BIOSPECIMEN COLLECTIONS Domain 1 describes the biospecimen collection activities needed to identify and manage medical institutions (herein referred to as Clinical Sites) across the United States and Canada to engage and enroll cancer patients onto specific NCI biospecimen collection studies and to provide biospecimen collection kit services for the studies. NCI biospecimen collection studies will include collection of biospecimens and associated medical data. Some studies will require the identification of existing cancer biospecimen collections that meet quality and quantity metrics prescribed by the NCI and that are appropriately consented for use by NCI. The Contractor shall ensure these activities are conducted safely, efficiently, and in compliance with regulatory requirements as specified in IRB-approved NCI studies. DOMAIN 2: COMPREHENSIVE BIOREPOSITORY SERVICES, ACCREDITATION BY THE COLLEGE OF AMERICAN PATHOLOGISTS� BIOREPOSITORY ACCREDITATION PROGRAM (CAP/BAP), PATHOLOGY AND HISTOLOGY, TRAINING, QUALITY ASSURANCE, AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY. Domain 2 describes comprehensive biorepository services performed under biorepository accreditation by the College of American Pathologists� Biorepository Accreditation Program (CAP/BAP) and employing an onsite board-certified anatomic pathologist. Ability to provide expertise in tracking of pre-analytical variables and detailed inventory management for all biorepository activities per CAP/BAP requirements using an existing data management solution. Information technology support dedicated to biobanking operations, to include data and information collection, management, quality control and analysis. Ability to provide scientific expertise and leadership in biobanking activities including but not limited to appropriate processing of biospecimens into molecular analytes and appropriate biospecimen and analyte storage. Ability to provide administrative, program, and project support by performing administrative duties to provide continuity for office operations and procedures. DOMAIN 3: COMPREHENSIVE BIOREPOSITORY SERVICES, ACCREDITATION BY THE COLLEGE OF AMERICAN PATHOLOGISTS� BIOREPOSITORY ACCREDITATION PROGRAM (CAP/BAP), CLINICAL LABORATORY IMPROVEMENT AMENDMENTS OF 1988 (CLIA) AND PATHOLOGY SUPPORT Domain 3 describes comprehensive biorepository services with ability to provide services as described in Domain 2. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned

title: Finland – Bin-cleaning services – Jäteastioiden ja -säiliöiden pesupalvelut 2027
description: Pirkanmaan Jätehuolto Oy pyytää tarjouksia toimialueensa kiinteistöillä sijaitsevien jäteastioiden 140-770 l sekä säiliöiden 0,3-5 m3 pesupalvelusta. Pirkanmaan Jätehuolto järjestää alueensa kiinteistöille vuosittain pesukampanjoita, jolloin kiinteistön keräysvälineet pestään kertapesuna. Kampanjoita on vuodessa jäteastioille kaksi (kevät ja syksy) ja säiliöille kolme (kevät, kesä ja syksy). Pesu koskee vain niiden kiinteistöjen keräysvälineitä, jotka ilmoittautuvat mukaan pesukierrokselle. Perusurakkakausi on 1.4.2027 – 31.3.2029 (2 vuotta), jonka jatkoksi tilaajan ja urakoitsijan on mahdollisuus sopia yhden (1) vuoden optiosopimuksesta.

The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. A woman is presumed economically disadvantaged if she has a personal net worth of less than $750,000 (with some exclusions), her adjusted gross yearly income averaged over the three years preceding the certification less than $350,000, and the fair market value of all her assets is less than $6 million If claiming Woman Owned Small Business status, provide documentation that shows the company is at least 51% owned and controlled by one or more women, and primarily managed by one or more women that make long-term decisions for the business and hold the highest officer position in the business and work at the business full time during normal working hours. The women must be U.S. citizens. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. description: The Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs (CDMRP) seeks feedback to inform the fiscal year 2027 (FY27) Traumatic Brain Injury and Psychological Health Research Program (TBIPHRP) research focus areas and associated research funding opportunities. Although FY27 federal funds have not yet been appropriated, TBIPRP is collecting this information solely to support strategic program planning. This inquiry does not commit the program to incorporating this feedback into FY27 or any future TBIPHRP funding opportunities. The CDMRP wants to hear from all audiences, interested parties, and individuals from academia, industry, community and non-profit organizations, scientific and professional organizations, federal agencies, and the public. This RFI should not be construed as a solicitation or an obligation on the part of the TBIPHRP or the Department of War (DoW). BACKGROUND: The CDMRP represents a unique partnership between the U.S. Congress, the military, and the public to fund innovative and impactful medical research in targeted program areas. The CDMRP TBIPHRP�s vision is to optimize the prevention, assessment, and treatment of psychological health conditions and/or traumatic brain injuries. The TBIPHRP�s mission is to fund research to understand, prevent and treat psychological health conditions and/or traumatic brain injuries that accelerates solutions to improve the health and healthcare of Service Members, their Families, Veterans, and the American public. Appropriations for the TBIPHRP from FY21-24 and FY26 totaled $740.5 million. As of October 2026, FY27 funds for the TBIPHRP have not been appropriated. If appropriated, the CDMRP will utilize its two-tier review process https://cdmrp.health.mil/about/2tierRevProcess) to efficiently manage the TBIPHRP. title: DAF Advanced Aerospace Computing
description: DISCLAIMER & SPECIAL NOTICES This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for information, planning, and market research purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Prototype Proposals, or an announcement of a solicitation. Issuance of this notice does not obligate the United States Government (USG) to award a contract or other transaction agreement, nor does it commit the USG to pay for any information, preparation, or submission costs incurred. Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and must be clearly marked. All submissions will become USG property and will not be returned. The Government may utilize support contractors to assist in administrative and technical evaluation; appropriate non-disclosure provisions apply. 1.0 INTRODUCTION & PROGRAM OBJECTIVES The Department of the Air Force (DAF) is investigating commercial and public-private models to establish a world-class, purpose-built aerospace high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI) supercomputer. 1.2 Program Vision & Architecture Target Computational Footprint: A targeted deployment scaling up to an approximately 30,000-GPU-equivalent architecture optimized for complex tensor operations, physical AI, large model training, and dense scientific simulation. 2.0 PURPOSE OF THIS RFI The USG seeks feedback from high-performance computing providers, hyperscalers, data center infrastructure developers, private equity/infrastructure financiers, non-profit research institutions, and academic consortia. Specifically, this RFI is intended to gather empirical market data on: Financing viability and private debt/equity structuring for infrastructure on leased federal property. Technical approaches to hardware obsolescence and continuous refresh cycles. Electrical power, cooling, and phased facility footprint expansion within constrained site utilities. Multitenant security architectures accommodating commercial users alongside partitioned Secret/SAP defense workloads. 3.0 AREAS OF INQUIRY & QUESTIONNAIRE FOR INDUSTRY Respondents are requested to address the following topics. Organizations may respond to all sections or select only those aligned with their core expertise. 3.1 Private Financing, Capital Structure & Commercial Offtake Underwriting Requirements: What financing instruments, equity hurdle rates, and debt tenors are typically required for private capital to fund approximately $2.0B in computing equipment and physical data center facilities constructed on federally leased property? Lender Covenants & Real Property Rights: What specific leasehold security provisions, cure periods, and step-in rights do institutional lenders mandate in the event of performer/operator default? How are these reconcilable with standard federal leasehold termination rights? Pre-Revenue & Bridge Capital: What volume of upfront development capital is required to support consortium structuring, environmental permitting, utility interconnection, and detailed engineering prior to commercial revenue generation? What funding models have industry successfully used to cover this pre-revenue gap? Commercial Demand & Offtake Commitments: What is the viability of securing commercial take-or-pay or anchor-tenant commitments for non-defense capacity? What are the standard commercial pricing tiers for dedicated high-tier GPU capacity when public-interest priority preemption clauses are present? 3.2 Technical Architecture, Solvers & Hardware Lifecycle Aerospace-Optimized AI Architectures: How do modern GPU/accelerator architectures handle dense fluid dynamics, partial differential equation (PDE) solving, and physics-based ML models compared to traditional CPU-centric high-performance computing clusters? What solver porting constraints exist? Technology Refresh Models: High-density AI/ML hardware experiences economic and technical obsolescence within 3 to 5 years, while data center civil infrastructure operates on a 20+ year horizon. What operating and capital replacement models ensure hardware remains state-of-the-art without disrupting existing debt service? Workload Prioritization & Preemption Mechanics: Describe technical mechanisms (e.g., dynamic container migration, checkpoint-and-restore routines, automated queuing) that allow high-priority defense/research workloads to preempt commercial jobs without violating commercial Service Level Agreements (SLAs). 3.3 Site Utilities, Modular Deployment & Power Constraints Constrained & Phased Siting: The initial site envelope is constrained by an immediate local room power envelope (approx. 750 kW) scaling to a substation transformer capacity of up to 30 MW (with an ultimate target expansion of an additional 30 MW pad and battery storage). What modular or phased deployment architectures (e.g., containerized high-density modular pods) would industry recommend to deliver immediate compute while large-scale utilities are upgraded? Cooling & High-Density Thermal Management: What liquid cooling, direct-to-chip, or immersion systems are best suited for 100 kW+ high-density rack configurations where facility water access and local heat rejection infrastructure may be constrained? Resilient Utility Options: What microgrid, on-site energy storage (e.g., 250 MWh utility-scale battery), or power curtailment mechanisms does industry deploy to maintain high-availability computing on sites subject to grid or tariff curtailment? 3.4 Multi-Tenant Security, Enclaves & Data Isolation Classified Enclave Co-Location: Describe architectural and procedural frameworks that enable hosting unclassified commercial tenants alongside Secret, Top Secret, and Special Access Program (SAP) enclaves within the same physical campus or hall. Data Isolation & Weight Security: How does your system guarantee strict data segregation, tenant isolation, and protection against unauthorized model weight extraction or side-channel leakage across shared interconnect fabrics? Cross-Domain & Secure Ingestion: What proven cross-domain solutions (CDS) or guard mechanisms are recommended to transfer telemetry and synthetic flight test data between isolated classified flight programs and unclassified simulation environments? 4.0 INSTRUCTIONS FOR SUBMISSION 4.1 Response Format & Guidelines Executive Summary: Maximum 2 pages summarizing key findings, respondent corporate capabilities, and high-level feedback. Technical & Financial Response: Maximum 10 pages addressing the inquiries in Section 3.0. Supporting financial models, white papers, or architecture diagrams may be included as separate appendices. Format: Text documents in searchable PDF or Microsoft Word format; 12-point font, 1-inch margins. Financial models should be provided in Microsoft Excel format with functional formulas intact. 4.2 Submission Logistics Inquiries & Clarifications: Technical and administrative questions regarding this RFI must be submitted via email to the primary points of contact no later than 02 December 2026 following release. Submission Address: Responses must be transmitted via secure digital transmission or email to the Contracting Office point of contact identified in the formal posting. 5.0 ANTICIPATED NEXT STEPS & ENGAGEMENT Industry Engagement Sessions: Following receipt and review of RFI responses, the USG may invite select respondents to participate in one-on-one virtual or in-person clarification sessions.
